sources.title: ServiceNow company overview
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow publicly positions its cloud platform around enterprise workflows, automation, AI, productivity, and improved experiences for employees and customers.

sources.title: ServiceNow careers
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow careers material highlights customer impact, innovation, teamwork, inclusion, learning, and building technology that improves work.

sources.title: ServiceNow Code of Ethics and T.R.U.S.T. pillars
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow's Code of Ethics says trust is the foundation of its work and organizes expectations around transparency, responsibility, understanding, supervision, and teamwork, including accurate reporting and speaking up.

sources.title: ServiceNow Responsible AI principles
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow describes four responsible-AI principles: human-centered, inclusive, transparent, and accountable, and states that it achieved ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification for its AI management system across development and deployment.

sources.title: ServiceNow Global Impact and sustainability reporting
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow reports maintained 100% renewable electricity and carbon-neutral cloud, more than $33 million in total social investment, and a 33% volunteer participation rate, and frames integrity as a driver of trust.

sources.title: ServiceNow executive leadership
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow's leadership page lists a chief people and AI enablement officer, a chief learning officer, a chief workforce innovation officer, a global talent acquisition leader, and technology roles spanning cloud engineering, security, and AI engineering.

sources.title: How we hire at ServiceNow
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow describes three hiring stages: application with human review, interviews run on a prescriptive process with standard evaluation guides, and a hiring-team debrief; it says some roles include a technical coding assessment or presentation and that rounds vary by position.

sources.title: Using AI during the hiring process at ServiceNow
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow allows AI for preparation such as resume refinement and practice, but requires interviews, online tests, and technical challenges to be completed independently without AI or outside help, prohibits recording interviews, and says violations may lead to disqualification or a rescinded offer.

sources.title: Life at ServiceNow: purpose, values, and People Pact
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow frames its values as the actions and behaviors that guide employees to do the right thing in service of making the world work better for everyone, and describes a People Pact covering doing your best work, living your best life, and fulfilling the purpose together, supported by learning and mentorship programs.

sources.title: AI, Engineering, and Product teams
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow's AI, Engineering and Product careers page separates Forward Deployed Engineering, Platform and AI Engineering, Product Engineering, Developer Productivity, Global Cloud Services, Product Management, Quality Engineering and Global Customer Support, each with a distinct remit.

sources.title: Sales teams and customer-facing roles
sources.public_safe_signal: The sales careers page distinguishes account executives, customer excellence covering expert services, customer success and renewals, digital sales, solution consultants and strategic alliances, and names customer wow as a core value alongside Fortune 500 reach and high renewal rates.

sources.title: Early careers, Launchpad Academy, and ServiceNow University
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow's early careers page covers internships and co-ops, full-time early-career roles, a year-long Launchpad Academy for new hires, a Discover ServiceNow exploration program, free ServiceNow University courses and certifications, and platform careers across partner and customer organizations through RiseUp.

sources.title: ServiceNow Trust FAQ: shared responsibility, audit rights, and sub-processors
sources.public_safe_signal: ServiceNow's trust FAQ says customers are data controllers who must judge whether its data-agnostic security program fits their data, and that ServiceNow does not review customer content in ordinary operations. Customers can request audit materials covering ISO 27001/27018 and SOC 1/SOC 2 Type 2; new sub-processors come with an objection right; incident notices go to the support-portal contact.

culture_principles.name: Trust as the foundation
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow says trust underpins how it works with customers, people, partners, and communities, and turns that into five expectations covering transparency, responsibility, understanding, supervision, and teamwork.

culture_principles.name: AI that works for people
culture_principles.description: The company says its AI products should enhance human abilities and keep users in control, with human-centered, inclusive, transparent, and accountable principles guiding development.

culture_principles.name: Responsibility for the impact of the work
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow's ethics material says teams stand behind what they build, compete fairly, reject corruption, and accept responsibility for the impact of their work.

culture_principles.name: Measurable impact, not just commitments
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow publishes quantified global-impact measures such as renewable electricity, carbon-neutral cloud, social investment, and volunteer participation alongside its commitments.

culture_principles.name: Talent and AI enablement are connected
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow's executive structure combines people leadership with AI enablement, learning, and workforce innovation, suggesting capability building is treated as part of AI adoption.

culture_principles.name: Values assessed as observable behavior
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow says its values are the actions and behaviors expected of employees rather than slogans, and its hiring process evaluates skills and values together using standard evaluation guides.

culture_principles.name: Authentic evaluation without tool assistance
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow permits AI for preparation but requires interviews, tests, and technical challenges to be completed independently, saying it wants to see the candidate's own reasoning rather than a tool-assisted performance.

culture_principles.name: Wow our customers
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow's sales careers page names customer wow as a core value, describing it as active listening, relationship building, and going further than delivering the product, and ties that behavior to retention and referenceable customers.

culture_principles.name: Clarity about the platform's responsibility boundary
culture_principles.description: ServiceNow's trust material separates what the provider controls from what the customer must own: customers are treated as data controllers, are expected to assess whether the security program fits their data, and are responsible for keeping notification contacts current. The company presents this boundary as part of transparency rather than as an exception.

hiring_signals.signal: Substantiates claims with accurate, verifiable detail rather than broad assertions.
Explains how AI or automation keeps a human in control and where oversight must remain.
Raises concerns and challenges decisions constructively instead of staying silent.
Connects technical or product choices to measurable customer and business outcomes, including how impact will be tracked.
Shows inclusive collaboration, such as using varied perspectives or data sets to reduce bias in a decision.
Shows skills and values evidence in a format that survives a structured debrief, such as a coding exercise, presentation, or role walkthrough.
Explains their own reasoning without leaning on tools, and can say how AI was used only to prepare and how the output was verified.
Translates a non-linear background into transferable skills the role needs instead of apologizing for an unconventional path.
Connects daily work to the stated purpose and values with concrete behavior rather than reciting slogans.
For customer-facing technical roles, explains how they turned a customer problem into a configured solution and how adoption was measured.
For sales and solution-consulting roles, shows discovery, qualification, and multi-stakeholder work rather than product feature knowledge alone.
For early-career roles, shows self-directed platform learning through courses, certifications, or projects, and explains what they built or solved with it.
Separates provider-owned controls from customer-owned controls when discussing security, privacy, or compliance.

anti_signals.anti_signal: AI enthusiasm with no account of governance, oversight, or who remains accountable.
anti_signals.risk_reason: ServiceNow publicly grounds AI development in human control and accountability, so governance-free AI narratives miss a stated emphasis; this is a preparation signal, not an official disqualifier.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Citing metrics or outcomes that cannot be traced to a source, method, or verification step.
anti_signals.risk_reason: The company's ethics code explicitly ties transparency to honest statements and accurate reporting.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Avoiding disagreement or escalation when a concern is material.
anti_signals.risk_reason: ServiceNow's ethics framework says speaking up is encouraged and concerns are acted on, with leaders expected to listen.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Using AI-generated answers, outside help, or recording during a live evaluation.
anti_signals.risk_reason: ServiceNow states that evaluation stages must be completed independently and that violations may lead to disqualification or a rescinded offer; this is a published process rule rather than an inference.

anti_signals.anti_signal: A polished narrative with no concrete evidence of values-in-action or role-relevant skill.
anti_signals.risk_reason: The process pairs skills with values and relies on standard evaluation guides, so a story without observable behavior gives reviewers little to assess.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Assuming visa sponsorship or a fixed number of interview rounds.
anti_signals.risk_reason: ServiceNow says sponsorship is reviewed case by case for certain roles and that process and rounds vary by position, so candidates should confirm rather than assume.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Assuming a technical role at a platform company has no customer, support, or adoption dimension.
anti_signals.risk_reason: ServiceNow's engineering organization publicly includes Forward Deployed Engineering and Global Customer Support teams that work directly with customers, so a purely back-end framing misses part of the role landscape; this is a preparation signal, not an official disqualifier.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Treating sales as only quota-carrying account executives and ignoring solution consulting, customer success, renewals, or digital sales paths.
anti_signals.risk_reason: The sales careers page separates five distinct customer-facing role types with different remits.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Describing cloud security as wholly the provider's responsibility, with no account of customer configuration, data classification, or shared-responsibility boundaries.
anti_signals.risk_reason: ServiceNow's trust FAQ assigns controller duties and the sufficiency assessment to customers, and says the company does not review customer content in ordinary operations. Provider controls do not cover customer-side choices.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Treating an audit report or compliance badge as proof that a specific deployment is secure.
anti_signals.risk_reason: The FAQ presents audit materials as inputs for the customer's own review of whether the security program is sufficient. Certification scope and the customer's configuration still determine what the evidence covers.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Assuming a security-incident notice will reach anyone at the customer automatically.
anti_signals.risk_reason: The FAQ says notices go to the contact recorded in the customer's support portal, which makes maintaining that contact a customer responsibility.

signals: Connects platform or process choices to customer workflows, adoption, reliability, and measurable value.
Balances product, technical, commercial, and change-management constraints.

role_overlays.role_family: AI platform, governance, and responsible-AI roles
signals: Balances model or agent capability with control, transparency, and accountability mechanisms.
Explains how AI systems are evaluated, documented, and monitored after deployment.
Works across product, legal, security, and customer teams to set operating boundaries.
Designs for reliability, security, and scale in multi-tenant enterprise systems.
Shows depth in cloud engineering, platform operations, or data infrastructure.
Connects engineering choices to customer uptime and trust.

role_overlays.role_family: People, learning, and workforce innovation roles
signals: Connects talent development and learning to how the business adopts new technology.
Uses workforce data and measurement to evaluate program impact.
Designs enablement that respects employee experience and inclusion.

role_overlays.role_family: Engineering versus business and customer-facing hiring paths
signals: Engineering-track candidates should expect a coding assessment; business and customer-facing tracks more often involve presentations or role walkthroughs.
Both paths are evaluated against the same stated values and use standard evaluation guides.
Within engineering, candidates can distinguish platform, product, forward-deployed, quality, cloud, and developer-productivity work.
Within customer-facing work, candidates can distinguish account executive, solution consulting, customer success, renewals, and digital sales paths.
Builds in the customer's environment and can explain what became reusable across engagements.
Balances speed of proof with production reliability and handover.
Treats support conversations as input to product quality rather than as a separate function.

role_overlays.role_family: Sales, solution consulting, and customer success
signals: Shows discovery and qualification discipline rather than feature pitching.
Explains complex workflow solutions in business terms across multiple stakeholders.
Connects adoption and renewal outcomes to the customer's original problem.
Uses ServiceNow University courses or certifications to build demonstrable platform skill.
Can describe a project or lab where that learning was applied.
Understands that platform careers also exist across partner and customer organizations, not only inside ServiceNow.

role_overlays.role_family: Platform security, privacy, and compliance roles
signals: Maps shared-responsibility boundaries across provider, customer, and sub-processor controls.
Reads audit scope and certification coverage rather than treating a badge as proof.
Maintains notification paths and tests whether incident information reaches the right owner.
Assesses sub-processor and dependency changes for data, continuity, and exit risk.
